units.passage: Do not use AI-generated sources, as they are often formatted incorrectly or make up sources entirely.

units.passage: NDSU supports 62+ research groups using AI across all colleges.

units.passage: A good classroom policy provides guardrails without inhibiting creativity.

units.uncovered_note: A design principle for course AI policies: guardrails without inhibiting creativity.

units.passage: As we step further into a digital world, it is also crucial to value creativity, empathy, and the unique perspectives that only human experiences can bring.

units.uncovered_note: Asks for balance between AI and human experience rather than warning of displacement. / Rationale that human creativity, empathy and lived perspective should be valued and balanced against AI's benefits.

units.why: "AI systems must be financially transparent and prevent misuse" is a resource-use rule on AI systems; it fits no type (not use, access or privacy), so UNCOVERED.

units.passage: Ensure the committee has expertise in evaluating AI grading methodologies.

units.uncovered_note: Grade-appeal committees should have expertise in evaluating AI grading methods. / Grade-appeals committees should have expertise in evaluating AI grading methods.

units.uncovered_note: Certificate eligibility and prerequisites should be adjusted for AI courses.

units.why: "Consider distance learning opportunities for AI courses while maintaining the requirement for completing at least 50% of coursework in residence" is program administration for AI courses; UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Distance learning for AI courses is considered within the 50% residence requirement.

units.why: "Highlight AI-related certificate programs on transcripts" concerns registrar practice for AI certificates; UNCOVERED.

units.why: "Define new prerequisites for AI courses" is graduate program administration; UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: New prerequisites are defined for graduate AI courses.

units.why: "Review policies for transferring credits, especially for AI courses from other institutions" is credit transfer administration; UNCOVERED.

units.passage: For faculty who teach from a common syllabus that includes the use of AI, faculty are expected to follow the agreed upon syllabus learning outcomes
units.why: "For faculty who teach from a common syllabus that includes the use of AI, faculty are expected to follow the agreed upon syllabus learning outcomes" binds instructors of common syllabi; no type covers common-syllabus rules.

units.uncovered_note: Instructors who teach from a common syllabus that includes AI use follow the agreed syllabus learning outcomes.

units.passage: Invest time in identifying your organizational goals and objectives for using the AI system and testing it to make sure it accomplishes those goals.
units.why: "Invest time in identifying your organizational goals and objectives for using the AI system and testing it" is advice to set goals and test before using AI; no type fits, so UNCOVERED.
units.fit_note: Staff should set goals for an AI tool and test it before use.
units.uncovered_note: Staff should define their goals for using an AI system and test that it meets them.

units.passage: To maintain a culture of academic integrity, students are to refrain
units.policy: The restriction on AI tools is meant to maintain a culture of academic integrity.
units.why: "To maintain a culture of academic integrity" gives the reason for the ban; it explains the rule rather than adding a requirement, so it is rationale.
units.uncovered_note: Integrity-culture rationale for restricting AI; not about skill-building (P41) or an institution-wide framework (P56).

units.passage: You will be provided with examples of how to cite your use of this tool in your writing.
units.policy: Students are provided with examples of how to cite their use of the AI tool in their writing.

units.passage: Use beyond these purposes is not permitted and must be disclosed when required.
units.policy: Use beyond the purposes listed in the assignment instructions is not permitted.
units.why: "Use beyond these purposes is not permitted" bans AI use outside the listed purposes; this is not a ban on producing submitted work (P19) or a default ban (P01) and is specific to the limited tier.

units.passage: Start with the syllabus and assignment instructions.
units.policy: Students start with the syllabus and assignment instructions to learn what AI use is allowed.

units.uncovered_note: Students are told to start with the syllabus and assignment instructions to learn what is allowed.

units.passage: Cite real authors and publications accurately
units.why: "Cite real authors and publications accurately" is an item in the list that follows "AI tools can sometimes reproduce or closely paraphrase copyrighted material without citation", so it tells students to credit human sources properly. P24 is about disclosing AI use and P31 about verifying AI output; neither says this, so it is UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Students are told to cite real authors and publications accurately, a general citation-accuracy duty that is neither disclosure of AI use (P24) nor verifying AI output (P31). Coder notes kept: Concerns citing real sources accurately, not verifying AI output in general. | Concerns accurate citation of real sources, not disclosure of AI use.

units.passage: Users have the right to know when they are using generative AI tools. This knowledge can encourage informed decisions about whether to engage, share, or rely on the generated content.
units.why: The text says 'Users have the right to know when they are using generative AI tools'. That is a transparency right about AI presence, not any listed type (P47 covers instructors disclosing their own AI use), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Users have a right to know when they are interacting with generative AI so they can make informed choices (informed consent).

units.passage: Reimagine the future of learning and teaching with AI by advancing leading-edge pedagogical practices and classroom environments that foster creativity and engagement
units.why: The committee will 'Reimagine the future of learning and teaching with AI' by advancing 'leading-edge pedagogical practices'. It is an institutional aim to advance AI-enabled teaching, not a default rule about who may use AI, so P02 does not fit and it is UNCOVERED. Informs, general, encourage.
units.uncovered_note: The committee aims to advance leading-edge AI-based pedagogical practices and classroom environments that foster creativity and engagement. (Coder A had mapped it to P02, noting it is an aim to advance AI-enabled pedagogy, not a default rule about student or instructor use.)

units.passage: They will likely become pervasive, ubiquitous, and embedded within the common applications used by students, scholars, and professionals of many types.
units.why: Predicts AI will be 'embedded within the common applications' students use. It is a forecast, not a rule on embedded-tool use, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Forecast that AI will become pervasive and embedded in everyday applications, offered as context for rethinking teaching. / Warns that AI will be embedded in common applications and tools students use; no rule attached.

units.uncovered_note: AI as an accessibility aid for people with disabilities (captions, descriptions, adaptive support), plus accessibility risks of AI output. / Describes AI as an accessibility aid; no rule about access or accommodations.

units.why: "will establish an AI Governance Council ... to oversee policy implementation, review incidents, and evaluate new technologies" creates a body. units.uncovered_note: Names which office owns interpretation, monitoring and enforcement of the AI guidelines. | Assigns who interprets, monitors and enforces the AI guidelines.

units.passage: Review the academic integrity policy provided in each of your course syllabi.

units.uncovered_note: Students are told to read the academic integrity policy in each course syllabus.

units.uncovered_note: Permits using AI output as an object of critique, comparison or analysis in course activities.

units.why: Says easier access to AI tools may be used 'whether intentionally or inadvertently' to submit work not the student's own; context-setting problem statement, informs. No type fits a background statement that misuse may be inadvertent, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: States that AI misuse may be intentional or inadvertent as background to the guidance, without setting a rule.

units.policy: A supportive faculty presence can help serve as a resource to students in the class and deter academic integrity issues.

units.uncovered_note: Rationale that instructor presence during in-person exams deters integrity violations and serves students as a resource.

units.uncovered_note: AI use is required for a given assignment or project, with instructions on how.

units.passage: AI use in at least one manner will be considered mandatory for the project
units.why: 'AI use in at least one manner will be considered mandatory for the project' requires AI use in a project. It is addressed to students, during work, with 'will be considered mandatory' as must. No type covers required AI use (P35 is redesign, P02 a default), so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: AI use is required for a given assignment or project, for this course's empathy project.

units.passage: Some assignments will require full use of AI to complete the assignment.

units.uncovered_note: Some assignments require full use of AI, to train students in using AI tools.

units.passage: AI may be utilized to help you analyze your data.

units.uncovered_note: AI may be used to analyze research data, such as finding themes in qualitative data.

units.passage: As an AI-enhanced course, you will leverage AI tools to refine research questions, analyze data, generate insights, and enhance your overall research methodology, ensuring you are well-equipped with modern research skills and technologies.
units.why: 'As an AI-enhanced course, you will leverage AI tools to refine research questions, analyze data, generate insights' builds AI use into the course's work. units.uncovered_note: Presents AI as accessibility support for learners with diverse needs; a benefit claim, not an access rule.

units.uncovered_note: The course is built around AI use: the class uses AI to generate text, images and music.

units.passage: Resources from the Teaching and Learning Resource Center Resources from the Drake Institute for Teaching and Learning
units.why: The 'Learn More' list points readers to the Teaching and Learning Resource Center, the Drake Institute and the Committee on Academic Misconduct. It offers resources but no rule, and no existing type covers a pointer to teaching-center and integrity-committee resources, so UNCOVERED.

units.passage: For the purposes of this rule, attempt shall be defined as conduct that, if successful, would constitute or result in the prohibited conduct. (A) Academic misconduct. Any activity that tends to compromise the academic integrity of the university or subvert the educational process. Examples of academic misconduct include, but are not limited to: (1) Violation of course rules and/or assignment guidelines as contained in the course syllabus or other information provided to the student; (2) Knowingly requesting, providing, and/or receiving unauthorized information, materials, and/or assistance during academic activities; (3) Possession and/or use of unauthorized information, materials, and/or assistance during academic activities; (4) Submitting plagiarized work for an academic requirement.
units.why: The rule defines 'attempt' as 'conduct that, if successful, would constitute or result in the prohibited conduct', so attempted unauthorized AI use is also punishable. No type covers attempt liability, so UNCOVERED.
units.uncovered_note: Attempting prohibited conduct, including unauthorized AI use, is treated the same as completing it.

units.passage: Campus Resources Teaching AI raises important questions about learning goals, assessment, authorship, and academic integrity.
units.why: The opening sentence frames AI as raising "important questions about learning goals, assessment, authorship, and academic integrity" but sets no rule; no type captures a bare framing of issues, so it is UNCOVERED rather than stretched.
units.uncovered_note: Names the issues AI raises (learning goals, assessment, authorship, integrity) as context for instructor choices, without a rule.

units.fit_note: Requires disclaimers on AI outputs in educational settings about limits, assumptions and bias; not a student verification duty. / Other coder's UNCOVERED note: AI outputs in educational settings must carry disclaimers on limitations, assumptions and biases and on the human user's role.
units.uncovered_note: AI products or outcomes generated in educational settings must carry disclaimers about the AI system's limitations, assumptions and biases and the human user's responsibility for interpreting them.

units.passage: Collaboration and Partnerships : Forge partnerships with industry stakeholders, government agencies, and academic institutions to exchange knowledge, share best practices, and stay abreast of emerging trends in AI technology and policy. units.fit_note: Institution-level community forums, not instructors explaining rules to students. / Other coder's UNCOVERED note: The university holds discussions and forums with students, staff and community on AI ethics, privacy and societal impact.
units.uncovered_note: The university engages students, faculty, staff and the wider community in discussions and forums on AI ethics, privacy and societal implications, and works with local stakeholders on community concerns.

units.passage: You can always grade against your criteria.
